method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited locator address was checked to begin an instruction of its decoded function, and the operands, name literals, vftable cells, constants and call targets named in the claims were compared with those listings by a second pass. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions and the whole image for dword references, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json and the observations of one retained capture. Script argument counts, result counts and shapes come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of seven native registrations: the CutScene natives _play, _replay and _skip, the WorldMaster native _getPendingCutSceneActor and the PlayerBase natives _getCutSceneReplaySnpcNickname, _getCutSceneReplaySnpcCoordinate and _getCutSceneReplaySnpcPersonality. Each row gives the registration site, the receiver type check, the declared argument and return lists, the branches, the reads, the effects on client state, the failure behavior and the yield behavior. The record also gives the argument split of the open list, the PlayingResumeChecker, the completion routine, the serverbound 0x00CE record and the host contract of a fade-through host. Client-side contracts do not establish cut scene content, scene element behavior or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/achievement_target_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/player_misc_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers and the yield request. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Order 83 of the PlayerBase switchboard is _getCutSceneReplaySnpcSkin, whose row is in manifests/player_misc_native_call_contract.json.

objectChain.definition: The callbacks reach one client object through 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04. With R the address that routine returns, X is the dword at R and Y the dword at X +0x04, the chain of manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json. P is the dword at Y +0x08 and V the first dword of P. Z is the dword at V +0x4C8, which 0x004D7330 returns. The fade element F is the dword at V +0x4CC, which 0x004D7340 returns. 0x004D6D10 sends through the dword at V +0x174EC.

facts.claim: 0x004D7330 returns the dword at its receiver +0x4C8 and 0x004D7340 returns the dword at +0x4CC. 0x004D6D10 loads the dword at its receiver +0x174EC and jumps to 0x004E0240, or returns 0 when it is null. 0x004E0240 loads the dword at +0x234 of that object and its +0x70, then calls 0x00DAE010.
0x0076D610, 0x0076D820 and 0x0075B200 each load the first dword of their receiver, the object at Y +0x08, before 0x004D7330. 0x0076D610 posts through 0x004D6D10 on that first dword.

That V is the Application::Main::RaptureElementContainer of the fade contract and that Z is a scene player element follows from the shared V offsets and the state dword at Z +0x98. Neither class name was read from RTTI for Z.

0x006EED90 is a ret 0xC routine that the callback calls with the CutScene receiver in ECX. It takes the argument object A, which is the dword at ExecuteParameters +0x10, and two output vectors. It reads the cell vector W as the dword at A +0x04, with begin at W +0x04, end at W +0x08 and 16 byte cells (0x006EEE08). It reserves 8 elements of 4 bytes in the first through 0x007222D0 and 5 elements of 0x54 bytes in the second through 0x00721720, and both grow on append through 0x00723C60 and 0x00723100.

It walks the cells from index 0 in three runs. A run of cells with tag 2 (bool) builds one 32 bit mask with bit i set for a true cell at index i (the shift count is taken modulo 32) and appends the mask once as one int element when the run ends. A run of cells with tag 0 (int) appends each int, read through 0x005819A0, to the first vector. A run of cells with tag 3 (Utf8String) appends each string, read through 0x0071CE70, to the second vector. A cell whose tag does not continue the walk ends it and the remaining cells are ignored. Float, Nil and control cells are never appended.
The failure route 0x009D22B4 is reached when the cell vector bounds check fails. A tag mismatch inside a run cannot occur because each reader runs only after its own tag test.

The runs match the shape of the replay arguments that populacecutsceneplayer passes (xivl-client-scripts:docs/cutscene-replay-skip-contract.md, section Inn replay selection): columns 8 through 15 of a cutReplay row. The mapping of those columns to the three runs was not traced.

facts.claim: The constructor 0x00713030 stores the vftable 0x00FD51AC, zero at +0x04, a zero byte at +0x08 and the waiting result, the dword at 0x0130CECC, at +0x0C. The vftable cells are slot 0 0x007130A0, slot 1 0x00713090 and slot 2 0x007491F0.

Slot 1 0x00713090 copies the dword at +0x0C into its output cell and ends with ret 0xC. It tests nothing, so the result stays waiting until a writer replaces +0x0C. The done result is the dword at 0x01377ECC, which s_FadeResumeChecker stores once its flag clears.
Slot 2 0x007491F0 pushes the bool at +0x08 through 0x00748870 and then the int at +0x04 through 0x00584F70 on the return list, in the order of the declared list 0x0072BCA0.
That slot 1 is the poll and slot 2 the result push follows the fade checker, whose slot 1 is the poll at 0x0071C7B0, and the push pair of slot 2.

completion.signature: CutScene member, ret 0xC, arguments (context handle, bool, int)

facts.claim: 0x006FBC50 takes the handle that 0x00CC7510 accepts as its first argument, a bool as its second and an int as its third. A true bool first calls 0x006FB9C0 with the handle. It then stores (bool == 0) at receiver +0xC0, stores the int at checker +0x04, the bool at checker +0x08 and the done result, the dword at 0x01377ECC, at checker +0x0C, and stores 0 at receiver +0x64. No instruction tests whether receiver +0x64 is null.

0x006FB9C0 returns without effect when the byte at receiver +0xC2 is 0. Otherwise it builds argument cells and calls the Lua function named by the literal _onFinalizeClip at 0x00FD462C and 0x00FD463C through 0x00CC7A90, in one branch gated on the byte at (receiver +0x68 object) +0x14.

0x006FBC50 then takes V and the area byte: 0x00763060 on Y returns 0 when the dword at Y +0x20 is 0 and otherwise the byte at +0xBB of the control stored at the first node of the list at Y +0x1C. It calls 0x00763DC0 on the dword at Y +0x08 with the address of receiver +0x6C, the byte at receiver +0xC1 and that area byte.

The only caller of 0x006FBC50 is the thunk 0x008A3910 at 0x008A3940. The thunk is a ret 0x10 routine. It casts its second stack argument from the type descriptor 0x01270964 to the CutScene descriptor 0x012C17AC through 0x009DA6CC and passes its first, third and fourth stack arguments on. Its only caller is the ret 8 invoker 0x0075D950 at 0x0075D973, and the address 0x0075D950 is stored once in .rdata, at the cell 0x00FDFBB8 of the vftable 0x00FDFB2C whose RTTI is .?AVLuaActorImpl@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@. That cell is slot 35. No caller of the slot was identified.

The CutScene vftable 0x00FD597C holds the only reference to the routine 0x006FCAA0, at the cell 0x00FD5990 (slot 5, offset 0x14). The control vftables that do not override the slot hold the base routine 0x006F6900 in it, for example WorldMaster 0x00FD5864 at the cell 0x00FD5878. 0x006FCAA0 is a ret 8 member taking the handle that 0x00CC7510 accepts and one more argument. It reads the dword at Y +0x08 as P and tests the byte at receiver +0xC0 and then the dword at receiver +0x64. When either is nonzero it calls 0x006FB9C0 with the handle, calls 0x0075B1B0 on P with the address of a stack cell filled through 0x0057AB60 from Y, clears the byte at +0xC0 at 0x006FCB25 and stores 0 at receiver +0x64 at 0x006FCB2C. No instruction on this path stores the done result into the checker or reads the checker, so a pending call is not resumed by it. Every path then calls the base routine 0x006F6900 with the same two arguments and, when the byte at receiver +0x5C is 0, calls 0x0075BE80 on the dword at Y +0x00.

The role of vftable slot 5 and its raiser were not traced. Reading the +0xC0 test as a deferred _onFinalizeClip, because a false completion skips 0x006FB9C0 and this routine runs it later, and reading the slot as a teardown of a cut scene that still holds a pending call, follow from the writes above only.

serverboundRecord.catalog: xivl-opcodes:opcodes.json MapServerbound entry _0x00CEHandler, and xivl-opcodes:data/client_opcode_semantics.json id c2s-00ce

facts.claim: Two builders write opcode 0x00CE and record size 0x38 into a stack record and send it through 0x004D6D10 with two zero arguments: 0x0076D610 for _play and 0x00763DC0 for the completion. In the stack record the code dword is at +0x00, the size dword at +0x04, the status dword at +0x18 and the 32 byte name field at +0x1C. The name field spans +0x1C through +0x3B.

The 0x38 byte record on the wire starts at stack record +0x08. This follows from the capture alignment. The 56 byte record follows the 16 byte subpacket header, so stack record +0x08 maps to subpacket +0x10, the status dword at stack +0x18 to subpacket +0x20 and the name at stack +0x1C to subpacket +0x24.

0x0076D610 zeroes the name field, copies the lesser of the name length and 0x1F bytes into it through 0x009D4600 and stores 0 as the status. 0x00763DC0 does the same copy and stores 1 as the status when its second argument is nonzero and 2 otherwise (neg, sbb, add 2). The four bytes after the name field are not written by either builder.

0x00763DC0 continues after the send only when its third argument, the area byte, is nonzero. It then runs a position comparison against a located control (0x00763EC1 onward). That branch was not traced.

xivl-captures:derived/payload_layouts.json, layouts.c2s.0x00ce, records 2 samples of 72 bytes whose body offset 16 (subpacket +0x20) takes the values 0 and 2, whose body offsets 20 through 27 are com0g105 followed by NUL padding to body offset 52 (subpacket +0x24 through +0x43), and whose 4 bytes at body offset 52 (subpacket +0x44) take the values 1 and 208. These match the status dword and the name field of the two builders. The xivl-captures cutscene-mechanic-book scenario file-inventory.csv lists 0x00ce in cutscene_book.pcapng (123,824 bytes), whose payload object is not part of the public xivl-captures tree. The order of the two samples (status 0 first, then 2) is an observation from that untracked object only.

0x004D7980 builds a ScenePacket with the type record number plus 0x15. The posts of this record are record number 0 (type 0x15) by 0x0055FFE0 with a 0xE8 byte record, record number 1 (type 0x16) by 0x00560050 with a 0xE8 byte record and record number 2 (type 0x17) by 0x00563C40 with a 4 byte record.

The dword at Z +0x98 takes the values 0, 1, 2 and 3. The writers of 1 are 0x0055FFBA, 0x0056003A, 0x00560091 and 0x005655A4, of 3 is 0x00563CC6, of 2 is 0x00563DE9 and of 0 are 0x00563DD3, 0x00563E38, 0x00565A4C and 0x00565A76. Only the writers in this record were read.
State 0 is idle, 1 playing, 2 finished with a replay name block stored and 3 skipping. The numbers are STATIC and the names are inferred from the guards of _play, _replay and _skip.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x0074F810 loads the callback 0x006FB830 at 0x0074F847, builds the return list bool and int through 0x0072BCA0 and the argument list of one Variable through 0x00728AC0, builds the non-const CutScene holder through 0x00726880 at 0x0074F88A, pushes the literal 0x00FD7F68 at 0x0074F8F9 and installs through 0x00CCCAD0. Its only caller is 0x00754816, the third registrar call of the CutScene switchboard 0x007547D0.

The callback passes the dword at ExecuteParameters +0x10, an argument object whose cell vector is at [+0x04], and two local vectors to 0x006EED90 on the CutScene receiver, which fills the int vector and the Utf8String vector. The split is recorded in framework.argumentSplit.

The callback resolves R through 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04, X as the dword at R and Y as the dword at X +0x04. It loads the dword at Y +0x0C and, when the dword at that object +0x110 is nonzero, calls 0x006F7CD0 on it, frees it through 0x009D1B17 and stores 0. The role of the object is untraced.

The callback then calls 0x0076D610 on the dword at Y +0x08 with the address of receiver +0x6C and the two vectors. That routine takes the first dword of the object as V, takes Z from 0x004D7330 (the dword at V +0x4C8), calls 0x0055FFE0 on Z with the file name characters and the vectors, and then posts the serverbound record 0x00CE through 0x004D6D10 on V.

0x0055FFE0 tests the dword at Z +0x98 against 0, calls 0x004D6820 on the object at Z +0x7C, builds a record of 0xE8 bytes through 0x00567930 from the name and the two vectors, posts it through 0x004D7980 with record number 0 and stores 1 at Z +0x98. 0x004D7980 adds 0x15 to the record number at 0x004D79D2.

After the manager call the callback allocates 0x10 bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs a PlayingResumeChecker with 0x00713030, stores it at receiver +0x64, clears the byte at receiver +0xC1 and requests a yield through 0x00CD2860 on ExecuteParameters +0x08 with the checker. No instruction tests whether receiver +0x64 already holds a checker.
A receiver that is not a CutScene fails the cast in the holder invoke 0x0071AA30 and the callback does not run. The cast target is the type descriptor 0x012C17AC.
The call-site index lists 1 site in 1 script, gamedata/cutscene_common line 1256. The count agrees with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

The bytecode scan shows the site passes the varargs of its enclosing function after the receiver and takes two results. The first result is compared with true to choose the path that hides the skip widget and, for one mode argument, calls _waitForMapLoaded on the local player. The function returns both results to its caller. xivl-client-scripts:docs/cutscene-replay-skip-contract.md records the same wait on the _play result in its skip actor binding section.

hostConsistency.reasoning: A host that runs the completion routine right after the call is consistent with the contract, because the callback only yields and the completion resumes it with a bool and an int. Resuming with true as the first result takes the path that the one script site tests for. The second result is an int whose meaning the client contract does not give, so its value is CALIBRATION. The retail client also posts the serverbound 0x00CE records of start and finish, and a host that omits them differs on the wire.

obligations: Read the open arguments as a bool run, an int run and a Utf8String run and ignore the rest.
Clear the skip byte, store a pending checker on the CutScene and yield until the completion routine runs.
Resume with the bool and the int that the completion supplies. The one script site tests the first result against true.
Behave as _play without the file name, without the Y +0x0C release and without a serverbound record.
Set the skip byte to 1, return nothing and do not yield. Do not resume the pending call from _skip.
Store the int and bool in the checker, mark it done, clear the pending pointer, set the +0xC0 byte to (bool == false) and call _onFinalizeClip for a true bool when the +0xC2 byte is set.
A host that completes at once is consistent with the contract when it resumes with a true bool. The value of the int is CALIBRATION.

When the +0xC0 byte or the +0x64 pointer is nonzero, apply the 0x006FB9C0 rule for _onFinalizeClip, call 0x0075B1B0 on P, clear +0xC0 and store 0 at +0x64 without writing the done result into the checker, so the pending call is dropped and not resumed. The caller of the slot and the retail condition that makes it run are untraced and the deferred finalize reading of +0xC0 is INFERRED.
Return the first CutScene whose +0xC0 byte is nonzero, and nothing when there is none.
Return the string at S +0x2C, the sign extended word at S +0x80 and the sign extended byte at S +0x83 for a MyPlayer receiver, and push nothing for any other PlayerBase.
A host that wants wire parity posts status 0 with the name when _play starts and status 2, or 1 after _skip, with the name when the completion runs.

ledgerCandidates.note: This record gives each of the seven natives a registration, a declared list and a body contract. A fade-through host satisfies _play, _replay and _skip by yielding and resuming with a bool and an int, and satisfies the getters by returning the stored book fields. The open questions name the values that stay CALIBRATION.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.

Callers, stores and loads come from a linear decode of the .text section and from dword scans of the image, so virtual and indirect references are not covered. An absent reference is not proof that none exists.

The MEASURED script counts agree with the shipped call-site index. The argument counts, result counts and call shapes come from a local bytecode scan of the installed client scripts and the scan is not tracked.
The payload layout observation covers two 72 byte 0x00CE subpackets. It does not establish the server reaction or the meaning of the statuses.
The scene element Z, its state values and the three ScenePacket records were read at their posts and guards only. The consumers were not traced.
The raiser of the CutScene completion was not identified. The bool and int that a retail finish supplies are open.
The area byte branch of 0x00763DC0, the role of the object at Y +0x0C +0x110 and the roles of the CutScene bytes +0xC2 and +0x68 were not traced.
The roles of fields come from native names, receiver names and neighbouring records and are INFERRED.
